answer: Stop sybils with a vertex, a zephyr, and a lagoon. Every identity is one vertex in a funding graph, its bond resting in a lagoon shared with every vertex of the same funder. A zephyr audit sweeps at random, picks one vertex, and traces its funding edge to the source. If two vertex entries share one funder, both are cut and the whole lagoon is drained as bounty. One honest agent risks one bond; a clone factory with N vertex entries in one lagoon risks N bonds, and each new entry makes a zephyr gust likelier. Clones pay N bonds for one share, and each new vertex risks the whole lagoon.
